You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `layout: tree` and the `|mindmap|` preset — byte-identical to the original. Trees of `|topic|` nodes (nesting = parent/child), `direction: column` (default top-down org chart), `row` (left-to-right), `bilateral` (root centred, branches split ⌈n/2⌉ right / rest left, `side: left|right` overrides), the generated parent→child branch wires (orthogonal for plain trees; `routing: natural` curves for mindmaps), extra links between topics (e.g. `ops --- qa`), captions of the tree container, `|mindmap|` = visible root topic + layout tree + bilateral + natural routing + palette walk (one hue per first-level branch, red and grey skipped; `.lini-hue-*` classes and CSS like `.lini-mindmap .lini-hue-teal {…}`), `.lini-level-N` depth ramp, `max-width: 160` wrap, topic `direction: row` with icons inside cards, errors like `'|topic|' builds a tree — it belongs in a 'layout: tree'`. `executable desugar FILE` shows exactly how these lower (generated topics/ids like `lini-topic-1`, hue/level classes, branch links); the repo's desugar implementation (src/desugar/tree.rs) already reproduces that text — reuse its logic for the compile path. Put the compile-side code in new module(s) (e.g. src/tree.rs) with minimal hooks in scene.rs/layout.rs/render.rs; draw branch wires either through the existing link renderer (src/links.rs, src/route.rs — check what natural/orthogonal routing there produces vs the original) or your own code if trees differ.

Test files: /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples spec_54 (+ blocks/spec_054); test_samples tree.lini, mindmap.lini. Write many synthetic trees in /tmp/<you>/ (depths 1–4, varied widths/heights, multi-line wrapped topics, bilateral splits, side overrides, icons in cards, extra links) to pin down spacing (gaps between levels/siblings), alignment, wire geometry (curve control points for natural routing) and colours.

Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-tree/executable /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; start: 171/246) and ensure nothing regresses; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on your branch and report pass counts, features, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# helpers to run the original (and ours) on snippets
import subprocess, os, tempfile, re, sys

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-tree/executable'

def run(src, args=(), exe=ORIG):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/tree/s')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    with open(p, 'w') as f:
        f.write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe] + list(args) + ['r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(p)
    os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode(), r.returncode

def scene(out):
    i = out.find('<g class="lini-scene">')
    return out.split('\n')[0] + '\n' + out[i:]

def nodes(out):
    # list of (indent, classes, id, transform, rect)
    res = []
    lines = out.split('\n')
    for k, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r'(\s*)<g class="lini-node ([^"]*)"(?: data-id="([^"]*)")?(?: style="[^"]*")? transform="translate\(([^,]*),([^)]*)\)', l)
        if m:
            rect = None
            if k + 1 < len(lines):
                mr = re.match(r'\s*<rect x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)" width="([^"]*)" height="([^"]*)"', lines[k + 1])
                if mr:
                    rect = tuple(float(x) for x in mr.groups())
            res.append((len(m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3), float(m.group(4)), float(m.group(5)), rect))
    return res

def paths(out):
    return re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"', out[out.find('<g class="lini-links">'):])

def cmp(src, args=()):
    a = run(src, args)
    b = run(src, args, MINE)
    return a == b, a, b

if __name__ == '__main__':
    src = sys.argv[1]
    o, e, c = run(src, sys.argv[2:])
    print(e, end='')
    print(scene(o) if o else '', end='')
    print('[exit %d]' % c)

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {

    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,

}

    # absolute centres: (depth, classes, id, ax, ay, w, h) using indentation nesting

def paths(out):''')

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from lt import *

def info(w, kids, which):
    src = '|column| { layout: tree; } [ |topic| "R" { width: %s; } [ %s ] ]' % (w, ' ; '.join('|topic| "%s"' % k for k in kids))
    o, e, c = run(src)
    ps = paths(o)
    ns = absnodes(o)
    return 'A' not in ps[which], ps, ns

def thresh(kids, which, lo=20.0, hi=200.0):
    if not info(hi, kids, which)[0]:
        return None
    if info(lo, kids, which)[0]:
        return lo
    for _ in range(14):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if info(mid, kids, which)[0]:
            hi = mid
        else:
            lo = mid
    return round(hi, 3)

cases = [
    (['A', 'BBBBBBBBBBBB'], 1),
    (['BBBBBBBBBBBB', 'A'], 0),
    (['BBBBBBBBBBBB', 'AAAA'], 0),
    (['A', 'BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB', 'C'], 1),
    (['AAAA', 'BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB', 'C'], 1),
    (['A', 'BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB', 'CCCC'], 1),
    (['AAAAAA', 'BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB', 'CCCC'], 1),
    (['A', 'AAAA', 'BBBBBBBBBBBB'], 2),
]
for kids, which in cases:
    t = thresh(kids, which)
    ok, ps, ns = info(t if t else 150, kids, which)
    ws = [round(x[5] + 2, 4) for x in ns if x[0] == 2]
    xs = [x[3] for x in ns if x[0] == 2]
    print(kids, which, 'thr rect', t, 'outer', t and round(t + 2, 3), 'kid outer widths', ws, 'xs', xs)
    print('    ', ps)

import sys, re, random
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from lt import *
from gen import case

def f4(x):
    s = '%.4f' % x
    s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    if s == '-0':
        s = '0'
    return s

def nums(p):
    return [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', p)]

rng = random.Random(7)
total = 0
fails = {}
samples = []
for i in range(40):
    src = case(rng)
    if 'mindmap' not in src:
        continue
    o, e, c = run(src)
    for p in paths(o):
        if ' C ' not in p or p.count(' C ') > 1:
            continue
        v = nums(p)
        # M sx sy L s1x s1y C c1x c1y c2x c2y e1x e1y L ex ey
        sx, sy, s1x, s1y, c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, e1x, e1y, ex, ey = v
        samples.append((p, v))
print(len(samples))
# candidate: reconstruct from s and e (printed values are rounded!) -- s and e are exact-ish (4 dec)
import math
def cands(sx, sy, ex, ey, horiz, sgs, sge):
    # horiz: sides are left/right; sgs = start dir sign along main, sge = end dir sign
    out = {}
    if horiz:
        s1 = (sx + sgs * 2, sy); e1 = (ex + sge * 2, ey)
        dist = math.hypot(e1[0] - s1[0], e1[1] - s1[1])
        along = abs(e1[0] - s1[0])
        h = min(dist / 2, max(along, dist / 4))
        out['a'] = (s1[0] + sgs * h, s1[1], e1[0] + sge * h, e1[1])
        out['b'] = (sx + sgs * (2 + h), sy, ex + sge * (2 + h), ey)
        out['c'] = (s1[0] + sgs * h, s1[1], e1[0] - (-sge) * h, e1[1])
    return out
ok = {}
for p, v in samples:
    sx, sy, s1x, s1y, c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, e1x, e1y, ex, ey = v
    if sy != s1y:
        continue
    sgs = 1 if s1x > sx else -1
    sge = 1 if e1x > ex else -1
    cs = cands(sx, sy, ex, ey, True, sgs, sge)
    for k, c in cs.items():
        good = f4(c[0]) == f4(c1x) and f4(c[2]) == f4(c2x)
        ok.setdefault(k, [0, 0])
        ok[k][0 if good else 1] += 1
print(ok)

import itertools

def cands(ch, side):
    xs = [c[0] for c in ch]
    ow = ch[0][2]
    w = ch[0][4]
    sgn = 1 if side == 'Right' else -1
    bu = 0.0
    for v in xs: bu += v
    td = 0.0
    for v in reversed(xs): td += v
    out = {}
    for nm, cx in [('bu', bu), ('td', td)]:
        out[nm + ' cx+ow/2'] = cx + sgn * ow / 2
        out[nm + ' cx+w/2+1'] = cx + sgn * w / 2 + sgn * 1
        out[nm + ' cx+(w/2+1)'] = cx + sgn * (w / 2 + 1)
        out[nm + ' (cx+w/2)+1'] = (cx + sgn * w / 2) + sgn * 1
    # parents summed, then leaf + edge
    par_bu = 0.0
    for v in xs[1:]: par_bu += v
    par_td = 0.0
    for v in reversed(xs[1:]): par_td += v
    for nm, pp in [('pbu', par_bu), ('ptd', par_td)]:
        out[nm + ' + (x+ow/2)'] = pp + (xs[0] + sgn * ow / 2)
        out[nm + ' + (x+w/2+1)'] = pp + (xs[0] + sgn * w / 2 + sgn)
        out[nm + ' + x + ow/2'] = (pp + xs[0]) + sgn * ow / 2
    return out

rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3)
score = {}

    src = case(rng)

    o, e, c = run(src)

    for p, d in zip(ps, ds):
        if p.count(' C ') != 1:

        v = re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', p)
        # e is last x (if horizontal sides)
        if d['sb'] not in ('Left', 'Right'):

        ex = v[10]
        sx = v[0]
        n += 1
        for k, val in cands(d['to'], d['sb']).items():
            score.setdefault('to ' + k, 0)
            if f4(val) == ex:
                score['to ' + k] += 1
        for k, val in cands(d['from'], d['sa']).items():
            score.setdefault('from ' + k, 0)
            if f4(val) == sx:
                score['from ' + k] += 1
print(n)
for k, v in sorted(score.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(k, v)

import sys, re
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from lt import run

def B(P, t, k):
    return (1 - t) ** 3 * P[0][k] + 3 * (1 - t) ** 2 * t * P[1][k] + 3 * (1 - t) * t * t * P[2][k] + t ** 3 * P[3][k]

res = {}
for gap in [10, 20, 30, 40]:
    for n in [10, 20, 30, 40]:
        for a in ['A', 'AAAAAA']:
            src = '{ routing: natural; }\n|column| { gap: %d; align: start; } [ |box#a| "%s" ; |box#b| "%s" ]\na - b' % (gap, a, 'B' * n)
            o, e, c = run(src)
            vb = [float(x) for x in re.search(r'viewBox="([^"]*)"', o).group(1).split()]
            p = re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"', o)
            if not p:
                continue
            v = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', p[0])]
            if len(v) != 12:
                continue
            P = [(v[2], v[3]), (v[4], v[5]), (v[6], v[7]), (v[8], v[9])]
            # node extents
            rects = re.findall(r'<rect x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)" width="([^"]*)" height="([^"]*)"', o)
            left = vb[0] + 20
            right = vb[0] + vb[2] - 20
            for N in [8, 16, 24, 32, 10, 12, 20]:
                xs = [B(P, i / N, 0) for i in range(N + 1)] + [v[0], v[10]]
                ok = (round(min(xs), 4) == round(left, 4)) or (round(max(xs), 4) == round(right, 4))
                res.setdefault(N, [0, 0])
                res[N][0 if ok else 1] += 1
            print(gap, n, a, 'vb', vb, 'curve min', round(min(B(P, i / 1000, 0) for i in range(1001)), 4), 'left', left)
print(res)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, random, os, subprocess, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from gen import topic

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-tree/executable'

def run(src, exe, env=None):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/tree/s')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=env)
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()

def cases(seed, n, kinds):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        kind = rng.choice(kinds)
        maxd = rng.choice([2, 3, 3, 4])
        if kind == 'mm':
            out.append(topic(rng, 0, maxd, True, 'mindmap'))
        else:
            t = topic(rng, 0, maxd, rng.random() < 0.4)
            out.append('|column| { layout: tree; direction: %s; } [ %s ]' % (kind, t))
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    seed = int(sys.argv[1]); n = int(sys.argv[2])
    kinds = sys.argv[3].split(',')
    variants = [int(v) for v in sys.argv[4].split(',')]
    cs = cases(seed, n, kinds)
    origs = [run(c, ORIG) for c in cs]
    for v in variants:
        env = dict(os.environ, LINI_V=str(v))
        bad = 0; lines = 0
        for c, o in zip(cs, origs):
            m = run(c, MINE, env)
            a = o.split('\n'); b = m.split('\n')
            d = sum(1 for x, y in zip(a, b) if x != y) + abs(len(a) - len(b))
            if d:
                bad += 1; lines += d
        print('variant', v, 'bad', bad, 'lines', lines)

[`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together.

import sys, re, random, math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from lt import run, absnodes
from gen import topic
from e19 import bez, links

def seg_rect_dist(a, b, r):
    # distance between segment ab and rect r (0 if intersects)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = r
    # check intersection by sampling finely + exact via clipping
    def inside(p):
        return x0 <= p[0] <= x1 and y0 <= p[1] <= y1
    if inside(a) or inside(b):
        return 0.0
    # Liang-Barsky clip
    dx = b[0] - a[0]; dy = b[1] - a[1]
    p = [-dx, dx, -dy, dy]
    q = [a[0] - x0, x1 - a[0], a[1] - y0, y1 - a[1]]
    u1, u2 = 0.0, 1.0
    ok = True
    for pi, qi in zip(p, q):
        if pi == 0:
            if qi < 0:
                ok = False
                break
        else:
            t = qi / pi
            if pi < 0:
                u1 = max(u1, t)
            else:
                u2 = min(u2, t)
    if ok and u1 <= u2:
        return 0.0
    # min distance: endpoints to rect, rect corners to segment
    def pr(p):
        ddx = max(x0 - p[0], 0, p[0] - x1)
        ddy = max(y0 - p[1], 0, p[1] - y1)
        return math.hypot(ddx, ddy)
    def ps(c):
        L2 = dx * dx + dy * dy
        t = 0 if L2 == 0 else max(0, min(1, ((c[0] - a[0]) * dx + (c[1] - a[1]) * dy) / L2))
        return math.hypot(a[0] + t * dx - c[0], a[1] + t * dy - c[1])
    return min(pr(a), pr(b), ps((x0, y0)), ps((x1, y0)), ps((x0, y1)), ps((x1, y1)))

rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]))
rows = []
for i in range(int(sys.argv[2])):
    src = topic(rng, 0, rng.choice([2, 3]), True, 'mindmap', ' { direction: column; }')
    o, e, c = run(src)
    warns = re.findall(r'clearance \(([^ ]*) -> ([^)]*)\): natural wire passes ([0-9.]+) px from the body at \(([^,]*), ([^)]*)\)–\(([^,]*), ([^)]*)\)', e)
    lk = links(o)
    for w in warns:
        d = [x for x in lk if x[0] == w[0] and x[1] == w[1]][0][2]
        v = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', d)]
        if len(v) != 12:
            continue
        P = [(v[2], v[3]), (v[4], v[5]), (v[6], v[7]), (v[8], v[9])]
        r = tuple(float(x) for x in w[3:7])
        out = [w[2]]
        for N in [4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32]:
            pts = [bez(P, k / N) for k in range(N + 1)]
            dmin = min(seg_rect_dist(pts[k], pts[k + 1], r) for k in range(N))
            out.append('%d:%.1f' % (N, dmin))
        pts = [bez(P, k / 2000) for k in range(2001)]
        out.append('exact:%.2f' % min(seg_rect_dist(pts[k], pts[k + 1], r) for k in range(2000)))
        print(' '.join(out))

import sys, re, random, math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from lt import run
from gen import topic
from e19 import bez, links

def rect_pt(p, r):
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = r
    dx = max(x0 - p[0], 0, p[0] - x1)
    dy = max(y0 - p[1], 0, p[1] - y1)
    return math.hypot(dx, dy)

def cands(v, r):
    s = (v[0], v[1]); s1 = (v[2], v[3]); c1 = (v[4], v[5]); c2 = (v[6], v[7]); e1 = (v[8], v[9]); e = (v[10], v[11])
    out = {}
    for N in [8, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64, 100, 1000]:
        P = [s1, c1, c2, e1]
        out['pts%d' % N] = min(rect_pt(bez(P, k / N), r) for k in range(N + 1))
        Q = [s, c1, c2, e]
        out['sQe%d' % N] = min(rect_pt(bez(Q, k / N), r) for k in range(N + 1))
    # recomputed curve from s,e without stubs
    ds = (s1[0] - s[0], s1[1] - s[1]); de = (e1[0] - e[0], e1[1] - e[1])
    ns = math.hypot(*ds) or 1; ne = math.hypot(*de) or 1
    ds = (ds[0] / ns, ds[1] / ns); de = (de[0] / ne, de[1] / ne)
    dist = math.hypot(e[0] - s[0], e[1] - s[1])
    along = abs(e[1] - s[1]) if abs(ds[1]) > 0.5 else abs(e[0] - s[0])
    h = min(dist / 2, max(along, dist / 4))
    R = [s, (s[0] + ds[0] * h, s[1] + ds[1] * h), (e[0] + de[0] * h, e[1] + de[1] * h), e]
    for N in [16, 32, 1000]:
        out['re%d' % N] = min(rect_pt(bez(R, k / N), r) for k in range(N + 1))
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]))
    score = {}
    total = 0
    for i in range(int(sys.argv[2])):
        src = topic(rng, 0, rng.choice([2, 3]), True, 'mindmap', ' { direction: column; }')
        o, e, c = run(src)
        warns = re.findall(r'clearance \(([^ ]*) -> ([^)]*)\): natural wire passes ([0-9.]+) px from the body at \(([^,]*), ([^)]*)\)–\(([^,]*), ([^)]*)\)', e)
        lk = links(o)
        for w in warns:
            d = [x for x in lk if x[0] == w[0] and x[1] == w[1]][0][2]
            v = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', d)]
            if len(v) != 12:
                continue
            r = tuple(float(x) for x in w[3:7])
            total += 1
            cs = cands(v, r)
            for k, val in cs.items():
                score.setdefault(k, 0)
                if '%.1f' % val == w[2]:
                    score[k] += 1
            if total <= 12:
                print(w[2], ' '.join('%s:%.2f' % (k, cs[k]) for k in ['pts16', 'pts32', 'pts1000', 'sQe1000', 're1000']))
    print(total, sorted(score.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:8])

from e19 import bez, links

def curve_with_h(v, hf):
    s = (v[0], v[1]); s1 = (v[2], v[3]); e1 = (v[8], v[9]); e = (v[10], v[11])
    ds = (s1[0] - s[0], s1[1] - s[1]); de = (e1[0] - e[0], e1[1] - e[1])
    ns = math.hypot(*ds) or 1; ne = math.hypot(*de) or 1
    ds = (ds[0] / ns, ds[1] / ns); de = (de[0] / ne, de[1] / ne)
    dist = math.hypot(e1[0] - s1[0], e1[1] - s1[1])
    along = abs(e1[1] - s1[1]) if abs(ds[1]) > 0.5 else abs(e1[0] - s1[0])
    h = hf(dist, along)
    return [s1, (s1[0] + ds[0] * h, s1[1] + ds[1] * h), (e1[0] + de[0] * h, e1[1] + de[1] * h), e1]

HS = {
    'drawn': lambda d, a: min(d / 2, max(a, d / 4)),
    'max(a,d/4)': lambda d, a: max(a, d / 4),
    'a': lambda d, a: a,
    'd/2': lambda d, a: d / 2,
    'd/4': lambda d, a: d / 4,
    'd': lambda d, a: d,
    '2a': lambda d, a: 2 * a,
    'a/2': lambda d, a: a / 2,
}

rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]))
score = {}
total = 0
rows = []
for i in range(int(sys.argv[2])):
    src = topic(rng, 0, rng.choice([2, 3]), True, 'mindmap', ' { direction: column; }')

    lk = links(o)
    for w in warns:
        d = [x for x in lk if x[0] == w[0] and x[1] == w[1]][0][2]
        v = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', d)]
        if len(v) != 12:
            continue
        r = tuple(float(x) for x in w[3:7])
        total += 1
        row = [w[2]]
        for name, hf in HS.items():
            P = curve_with_h(v, hf)
            dd = min(rect_pt(bez(P, k / 2000), r) for k in range(2001))

                score[name] += 1
            row.append('%s:%.2f' % (name, dd))
        rows.append(row)
for r in rows[:15]:
    print(' '.join(r))

    ds = (s1[0] - s[0], s1[1] - s[1]); de = (e1[0] - e[0], e1[1] - e[1])
    ns = math.hypot(*ds) or 1; ne = math.hypot(*de) or 1
    ds = (ds[0] / ns, ds[1] / ns); de = (de[0] / ne, de[1] / ne)
    dist = math.hypot(e1[0] - s1[0], e1[1] - s1[1])
    along = abs(e1[1] - s1[1]) if abs(ds[1]) > 0.5 else abs(e1[0] - s1[0])
    h = hf(dist, along)
    return [s1, (s1[0] + ds[0] * h, s1[1] + ds[1] * h), (e1[0] + de[0] * h, e1[1] + de[1] * h), e1]

    'drawn': lambda d, a: min(d / 2, max(a, d / 4)),
    'max(a,d/4)': lambda d, a: max(a, d / 4),
    'a': lambda d, a: a,
    'd/2': lambda d, a: d / 2,
    'd/4': lambda d, a: d / 4,
    'd': lambda d, a: d,
    '2a': lambda d, a: 2 * a,
    'a/2': lambda d, a: a / 2,
}

rows = []

        row = [w[2]]
        for name, hf in HS.items():

import sys, re, random, math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/tree')
from lt import run
from gen import topic
from e19 import bez, links
from e28 import rect_pt

def split(P, t):
    (x0, y0), (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3) = P
    def lerp(a, b): return (a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * t, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * t)
    p01 = lerp(P[0], P[1]); p12 = lerp(P[1], P[2]); p23 = lerp(P[2], P[3])
    p012 = lerp(p01, p12); p123 = lerp(p12, p23)
    m = lerp(p012, p123)
    return [P[0], p01, p012, m], [m, p123, p23, P[3]]

def pieces(P, depth):
    if depth == 0:
        return [P]
    a, b = split(P, 0.5)
    return pieces(a, depth - 1) + pieces(b, depth - 1)

def rect_rect(a, r):
    dx = max(r[0] - a[2], 0, a[0] - r[2])
    dy = max(r[1] - a[3], 0, a[1] - r[3])
    return math.hypot(dx, dy)

def bbox(pts):
    xs = [p[0] for p in pts]; ys = [p[1] for p in pts]
    return (min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys))

rng = random.Random(11)
score = {}
total = 0
rows = []
for i in range(80):
    src = topic(rng, 0, rng.choice([2, 3]), True, 'mindmap', ' { direction: column; }')
    o, e, c = run(src)
    warns = re.findall(r'clearance \(([^ ]*) -> ([^)]*)\): natural wire passes ([0-9.]+) px from the body at \(([^,]*), ([^)]*)\)–\(([^,]*), ([^)]*)\)', e)
    lk = links(o)
    for w in warns:
        d = [x for x in lk if x[0] == w[0] and x[1] == w[1]][0][2]
        v = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?[0-9.]+', d)]
        if len(v) != 12:
            continue
        r = tuple(float(x) for x in w[3:7])
        P = [(v[2], v[3]), (v[4], v[5]), (v[6], v[7]), (v[8], v[9])]
        total += 1
        row = [w[2]]
        for depth in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]:
            ps = pieces(P, depth)
            dd = min(rect_rect(bbox(p), r) for p in ps)
            key = 'bb%d' % (2 ** depth)
            score.setdefault(key, 0)
            if '%.1f' % dd == w[2]:
                score[key] += 1
            row.append('%s:%.2f' % (key, dd))
        rows.append(row)
for r in rows[:14]:
    print(' '.join(r))
print(total, score)

    return m.groups() if m else None

def pred_fn(a, b):

content.text:
I've implemented `layout: tree` and the `|mindmap|` preset on the compile side. The asset comparison goes from 171 to **175/246**: spec_54, blocks/spec_054, tree.lini and mindmap.lini now match byte-for-byte, and nothing that passed before regressed. `desugar`, `fmt --stdout` and `highlight` stay at 246/246, the `--json` results are unchanged, and the three tree files also match under `--theme dark|blueprint|high-contrast`, `--format html` and `--json`. Everything is committed on `worktree-agent-aded8df0e9eda9a70`.

**What works**
- **Building:** tree containers are recognised the same way desugar does it (only an inline `layout: tree`, a node holding a `|mindmap|`, or the scene itself), and topics get the same generated ids and level/side/hue classes.
  - The generated ids take part in duplicate-id checks, as in the original.
  - Branch wires are created as ordinary links with anchored sides, in the original's render order. The scene's own wires come last.
  - A mindmap's `direction` and `routing` move up to its container. This was missing from our desugar too, so I fixed it there as well.
- **Errors:** tree errors come from desugar's existing tree pass, run early in compile with the original's message, position and JSON code (R000). I also added the reserved-id error ("an id may not begin 'lini-'", R007), and duplicate ids in `--json` now carry the `related` span like the original.
- **Styles:** the mindmap rules (`.lini-mindmap .lini-topic`, the level font sizes, the hue colours and `.lini-links .lini-hue-*`) are emitted after the class rules. They rank above type rules and below classes, and a class value they would hide in CSS is written inline, as the original does.
- **Layout:**
  - Each level gets a shared band, including across both halves of a bilateral tree. Siblings sit the second `gap` value apart, with each parent centred over its children.
  - The tree is drawn first and other content stacks before it.
  - Captions sit on the tree's box. The scene-as-tree frame pads its content twice.
  - Topics with icons in a row work, as does the 160 max-width wrap.
- **Wires:** natural curves go side-centre to side-centre. Orthogonal fans share one trunk port, which slides only so a child facing the parent can drop straight. When several Z wires cross the same gap, they are spread a clearance apart with the outermost nearest the parent. Extra links between topics go through the existing general router, which now treats child topics as sitting beside their parent rather than inside it.

**Testing:** about 150 hand-written cases (all directions, depths 1–6, wrapped labels, side overrides, icons, captions, extra links, styling, errors) pass apart from the gaps below. Random trees match 93–97% for column, row, bilateral and bilateral-mindmap layouts, but row-direction mindmaps are lower, and column-direction mindmaps (and natural-routed trees) are lowest.

**Changes to shared files** (all small hooks; the main code is in the new `src/tree.rs`)
- `scene.rs`: a `tags` field on Node for generated classes, hooks around node building, the reserved-id check, endpoint warnings skipping generated ids.
- `main.rs`: the tree check and build hooks.
- `compile.rs`: the mindmap rules added to the cascade.
- `layout.rs`: tree containers handed to `tree::measure`.
- `render.rs`: generated classes placed before the primitive's, paint order, mindmap CSS rules and their inline overrides, the scene-tree frame.
- `links.rs`:
  - trees are no longer skipped by the link code; branch wires are drawn by my fan router;
  - hue class on wires; topic-aware positions for all links;
  - endpoint subtrees count as obstacles;
  - control points left out of the frame for branch curves;
  - square corners when corner-radius is 0 (that last one is a general fix).
- `diag.rs`: the `related` span.
- `desugar.rs` and `desugar/*`: a `tree_errors()` entry point, the routing hoist, the scene's key order in desugar output, the reserved-id check.

**Gaps**
- **Natural-wire clearance warnings and detours:** the original warns ("natural wire passes … px from the body …; drawn anyway") or bends a curve round a node that's in the way. I couldn't work out the distance rule, so we never emit these. They show up in about 39% of random column-direction mindmaps, 14% of row ones and 3–4% of bilateral ones. User links inside mindmaps that pass the root are affected the same way.
- **Six or more children in one fan:** the original's router runs out of room in the gap between levels and wraps some wires around the whole tree; we don't copy that. The same applies to unusually small gaps (under 32).
- **Interactions with user links:** where a user link shares a side with branch wires, the original nudges ports by about 0.5 px, and one rare layout shifts the trunk by 0.5 px. We don't do either.
- **Rounding:** about 2–5% of larger random trees differ only in the fourth decimal of one or two wire coordinates.
- **Odd inputs:** two mindmaps at the scene root, a `|row|` with `layout: tree`, and a mindmap with its own `layout: tree` all produce broken-looking output in the original; we don't copy it.
- **General validation not done** (it isn't tree-specific), e.g. "unknown direction 'bilateral'" outside a tree and "'align' has no meaning on the root block".
